set.fitNote: RESTATEMENT CORRECTION, 29 September (Christian). 04.a and 05.a carry the SAME basisEvidence — setup_guidance "Mark wide channels along both touchlines" — and 04.a's own fitNote already recorded "Holds only the contact in ‘runs along its touchline’ (same as 05.a)". They were two representations of one authored placement, not two competing authored values, and they collided on three channel elements by string inequality alone. The parenthetical is now a gloss beside the value rather than a second REQUIRED_RANGE contribution. Source, strictness, valueStatus and provenance are unchanged, and no engine semantics changed. "One channel on each lateral side" remains NOT held: touchline-adjacent does not say which touchline, and S2 has no side attribute (ledger).

items.why: two spellings of one authored placement were entailing two different values on S6, producing three collisions that were never a knowledge conflict. Making the parenthetical a gloss leaves one value, preserves both items and their shared source, and changes no engine semantics

set.fitNote: MARKED RELATIONAL 29 September, then TYPED AS DISTINCT_ON the same day once Christian adopted the assertion. The restatement had written one joint constraint as a per-element bound on O4, so it reached three separate object classes as three independent bounds — and three independently valid placements can still violate it. It is therefore NOT a bound on any one line, and contributes none. It is carried instead as a DISTINCT_ON assertion over the object collection: members differ pairwise on O4 and O5. No metric, no minimum separation — the source says explicitly "no separation distance" — no inferred geometry, and no line of its own. Realization chooses each placement against its own bound and is refused if the resulting SET violates it. Value, source and provenance are unchanged.

items.why: a joint constraint over a set of candidates had been flattened into a per-element bound, which both misstates the knowledge and would license a per-line realization freedom that cannot honour it. Typed as DISTINCT_ON so each placement stays freely choosable within its own bound while the set is checked jointly

set.fitNote: TYPED, 29 September (Christian). The authored value ">= 1 (no authored maximum)" already carries requirement RANGE, so the requirement kind was always quantitative; only the value string defeated the parser, which typed it QUALITATIVE and left the realization layer unable to check any value against a range it can plainly read. The number is MOVED from the prose into the typed field on the SD-86 precedent, not inferred: floor 1, and no maximum, exactly as authored. The prose value is unchanged so the source stays visible beside its typed form.

items.why: an explicitly authored numerical floor was sitting unreadable in prose; typing it changes no authored content and makes the bound checkable

set.fitNote: TYPED, 29 September (Christian). "1-2 (one or two)" typed as min 1, max 2. It remains SUPPORTING / PREFERRED_DEFAULT and is NOT converted into a required range: NEUTRAL-01.a states there is no authored maximum, so intersecting the two to [1,2] would turn a preference into a hard ceiling the knowledge never states. SD-90 already expresses the real relationship between a required bound and a preferred default; nothing new is needed and nothing is intersected here.

items.why: the preferred default is typed so it can be read, and deliberately left SUPPORTING so it cannot be mistaken for a required maximum

set.fitNote: TYPED, 30 September, on the SD-86 precedent and exactly as the neutral count was (C29c). The channel width was AUTHORED all along — requirement RANGE, basis AUTHORED, value "across-interval width about 6-10 m", from setup_guidance "(~6-10m wide depending on field size)". Only the value STRING defeated the parser, which typed it QUALITATIVE and left it bounding nothing a check could read. The numbers are MOVED out of the prose, not inferred: 6 and 10 are explicitly authored. The prose is unchanged beside the typed form, so "about" and the unauthored scaling both keep their own record. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not supply a scaling rule. S6 still records "no scaling rule for width; depending on field size gives no function", and that remains true — 6-10 m is a fixed range, not a proportion of the envelope. On a 40 x 30 m session it fits inside the 30 m across dimension, so it yields concrete geometry here; on an envelope where it would not, the proportional question is still open and is the owner decision returned rather than guessed at.

items.why: an explicitly authored numerical range was sitting unreadable in prose, so the channel width bounded nothing a spatial check could use. Typing it changes no authored content and makes the bound checkable; the absent SCALING rule is returned separately and not invented

item.fitNote: IE-D011 STATE_DEPENDENCY, whose question is "is the meaning or availability of information dependent upon the current functional state?". "When the count resets, the revealed state resets with it" is exactly that, and the reset is a detectable transition that changes what is worth doing — IE-D011’s integrity condition. Recording the reset as IE-D008 REVERSIBLE would in fact VIOLATE IE-D008’s own integrity condition, which requires later information to "refine rather than arbitrarily overturn the task".
